results.reasoning: (A) fullPassage says 'distant mountain' → distant. (B) 'I prefer something to be exact and precise' → exact. (C) 'it's an unusual medium' → unusual. Choice 3 = distant-exact-unusual.
(A) 'a strangely intimate moment' → strangely. (B) 'feature only polar animals' → polar. (C) 'It's less a physical thing' → physical. Choice 1 = strangely-polar-physical.
(A) 'A triangular outline' → triangular. (B) 'the hyper-real quality' → hyper-real. (C) 'you work light to dark' → dark. Choice 4 = triangular-hyper-real-dark.
② sculpture is wrong — original says 'a very realistic painting of one'. Sculpture (3D) contradicts painting (2D). Other markers (outline, safari, layer) all fit context.
③ approximate is wrong — original says 'exact and precise'. 'Approximate and precise' is self-contradictory. Other markers (mammals, exhibition, theme) all fit context.
① domestic is wrong — original says 'polar animals'. The exhibition was about polar/arctic animals, not domestic ones. Other markers (humpbacks, personality, species) all fit.

'unless they go on a _____ or an expedition' — safari pairs naturally with expedition as outdoor wildlife experiences. Vacation/voyage/journey are too generic and don't specifically relate to animal observation.
'it's an unusual _____ in hyper-realism' — medium is the art term for material/substance used (acrylic, oil, watercolor). Style/technique/approach describe methods, not materials.

'the hyper-real quality of her _____' — exhibits matches the context of displayed artworks in an exhibition. Paintings is close but not the original word; photographs is wrong (she paints); portraits is too narrow.
distant = far away, remote. 'Remote' is the closest synonym. Nearby is antonym, central is unrelated, familiar is metaphorically opposite.
aim = purpose, objective, goal. 'That's always been my aim' = 'That's always been my goal'. Hobby/regret/talent are semantically unrelated.
'lends itself to' = contributes to, is conducive to. Borrows is the opposite of lend. Reduces and opposes are semantically contrary.
unusual = not common, atypical. Antonym = typical (ordinary, normal). Remarkable and exotic are near-synonyms. Standard is close but typical is more precise.
polar = relating to the poles (Arctic/Antarctic). Antonym = tropical (relating to the tropics). Arctic/northern/frigid are similar to polar, not opposite.

(A) 'a very realistic painting of one' — painting = artwork (noun). (B) 'painting herself into a corner' — idiomatic expression meaning to put oneself in a difficult situation. Choice 1 correctly identifies both meanings.
'a public display of works of art or other items of interest, typically in a museum or gallery' = exhibition. Expedition=exploration, experiment=scientific test, expression=conveying feelings.
'there's something _____ (reflect)' — past participle 'reflected' modifies 'something'. Structure: something + p.p. = something that is reflected.
'the planet's most _____ (beleaguer) mammals' — past participle used as adjective before noun. 'Most beleaguered' = superlative form meaning most besieged/troubled.

'people can feel they're _____ with the animal, rather than looking through a lens' — face to face implies direct, intimate encounter. In contact/in conflict/side by side don't convey the direct confrontational visual experience.

'Light value on top of dark values kind of gives the impression of being in _____' — three dimensions. The passage discusses how layering light over dark creates depth perception, giving a 3D illusion.
